notes:
I've put together verse notes for most of 2 Samuel 19:23–43, drawn mainly from older commentaries on biblehub and studylight and from enduringword and preceptaustin. There are gaps. The full Enduring Word and Precept Austin pages cut off partway through, so some verses rely only on search snippets. I found nothing on vv. 33, 38 or 42 beyond the bare text. Wesleyan, Pentecostal-specific, Orthodox, bibleodyssey and NET-note material didn't turn up, and neither did any prosperity, word of faith or hyper-grace teaching on this passage.

## 1. The traditional reading, verse by verse

**v. 23 (David spares Shimei under oath)**
- **Mercy (Guzik, enduringword):** David spared the man who had cursed him bitterly. Guzik says he could forgive because he felt secure, knowing God had given him the throne. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-samuel-19/
- **Henry:** Having received God's mercy himself, David was inclined to show mercy: "Those that are forgiven must forgive." https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-samuel/19-23.html
- **Christ-centred reading (biblehub study notes):** David's "You shall not die" echoes what Nathan told David in 2 Samuel 12:13. The notes see it as a pattern of the gospel, where those who deserve death receive life by the king's word. https://biblehub.com/2_samuel/19-23.htm
- **The later problem (1 Kings 2):** On his deathbed David told Solomon to deal with Shimei, and commentators split over whether that broke the oath. See section 2.

**v. 24 (Mephibosheth's neglected appearance)**
- **Meaning:** He hadn't washed his feet, trimmed his moustache or washed his clothes. Cambridge Bible calls these outward signs of extreme grief. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_samuel/19-24.htm
- **"Beard":** The Hebrew word means only the moustache. Barnes says the verse helps clear Mephibosheth of suspected disloyalty. Same URL.
- **"Son of Saul":** This means grandson, as in 2 Samuel 4:4 (Benson). Same URL.
- **Not dressed like a claimant (preceptaustin):** His untidiness shows he wasn't trying to look like a king, as he would have if he wanted the throne. https://www.preceptaustin.org/2-samuel-19-commentary

**v. 25 ("He came from Jerusalem")**
- Some writers keep the text as it stands. They think Mephibosheth had taken refuge on his family estate near Gibeah during the revolt and came from there to Jerusalem. Either way, his mourning shows loyalty. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_samuel/19-24.htm

**v. 26 (Ziba deceived me)**
- **Text note (ISBE, quoted by preceptaustin):** Following the Greek and Syriac versions, it reads "Saddle me the ass," so Mephibosheth asked Ziba to saddle it, instead of the Hebrew "I will have saddled." https://www.preceptaustin.org/2-samuel-19-commentary
- **F.B. Meyer:** Ziba took the donkey Mephibosheth meant to ride, then claimed his master hoped to get back Saul's throne. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/fbm/2-samuel-19.html

**v. 27 (slander; "like the angel of God")**
- **Preacher's Homiletical:** Mephibosheth had probably found out about the slander long before, once Ziba started using David's grant against him. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/phc/2-samuel-19.html
- On the "angel of God" phrase itself I found the text quoted but no comment.

**v. 28 ("all my grandfather's house deserves death")**
- **Preceptaustin:** He means David could have wiped out the whole family. https://www.preceptaustin.org/2-samuel-19-commentary
- **Guzik:** He didn't defend himself, because David had already given him more than he deserved. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-samuel-19/
- **Pulpit Commentary:** He could bear this meekly because he was humble, thankful and devoted to the king. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/2-samuel-19.html

**v. 29 ("You and Ziba divide the land")**
- **Henry:** David was restoring his first arrangement. Mephibosheth still owns the land and Ziba farms it, paying rent. Henry adds that Ziba went unpunished for his lies. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-samuel/19-29.html
- **Constable:** David may have split the fields to find out who was telling the truth, much as Solomon offered to divide the baby. Same URL.
- **Guzik:** David didn't take back his promise to Ziba, but he did cut down Ziba's reward. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-samuel-19/
- Many others call the ruling unjust; see section 2.

**v. 30 ("Let Ziba take it all!")**
- **Guzik:** David's reign mattered more to Mephibosheth than his own wealth. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-samuel-19/
- **Henry:** A good man can cheerfully accept his own losses while he sees Israel at peace. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_samuel/19-29.htm
- **Jamieson-Fausset-Brown:** His generous, unselfish spirit was worthy of his father Jonathan. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_samuel/19-24.htm

**vv. 31–32 (Barzillai)**
- **Guzik:** Barzillai used his wealth for God's servant and God's cause. He was "rich toward God" (Luke 12:21). https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-samuel-19/
- **Preceptaustin:** He gave in faith, not knowing whether David would survive, and the lesson is that no one is too old to be used by God. https://www.preceptaustin.org/2-samuel-19-commentary
- **Pulpit:** He provided food "with some help from others" while David's army camped at Mahanaim. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/2-samuel-19.html

**vv. 34–35 (too old for court life)**
- **Clarke:** Barzillai was frail as well as old. Food and singers were a main part of royal banquets. https://studylight.org/commentaries/acc/2-samuel-19.html
- **Preceptaustin:** His questions mirror Ecclesiastes 12:1–7, on the fading of pleasures in old age. https://www.preceptaustin.org/2-samuel-19-commentary
- **Henry:** The old should learn from Barzillai to be dead to the pleasures of the senses. He would rather burden his own house than the king's. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/2Sa/2Sa_019.cfm

**v. 36 ("Why should the king repay me?")**
- **Guzik:** Barzillai gave from a right heart, not for reward. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-samuel-19/
- **Henry:** He played down his own service and praised the king's generosity. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/2Sa/2Sa_019.cfm

**v. 37 (Chimham)**
- **Who Chimham was:** Most commentators say Barzillai's son, citing 1 Kings 2:7. Clarke (via Guzik) and Coffman, who cites Josephus, both say so. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-samuel-19/ and https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/2-samuel-19.html
- **Dying at home:** The Pulpit says Barzillai wanted death to find him in his family's old home, near his parents' graves. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/2-samuel-19.html
- **"Habitation of Chimham":** Clarke ties Jeremiah 41:17's "habitation of Chimham" near Bethlehem to land David may have given him. https://studylight.org/commentaries/acc/2-samuel-19.html

**v. 39 (kiss and blessing)**
- **Clarke:** The kiss was a sign of friendship and farewell. The blessing was a prayer for his prosperity. https://studylight.org/commentaries/acc/2-samuel-19.html
- **Preceptaustin:** Barzillai's crossing was largely symbolic of David's return to his kingdom. https://www.preceptaustin.org/2-samuel-19-commentary

**vv. 40–43 (the tribes quarrel)**
- **Bridgeway:** Judah's eagerness stirred up jealousies between the tribes that would later break up the kingdom. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-samuel/19-29.html
- **"Ten shares" (Gill):** Ten tribes, counting Simeon as part of Judah. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-samuel/19-43.html
- **"Ten shares" (Pulpit):** The tribe that drops out is Simeon, not Benjamin. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_samuel/19-43.htm
- **Seeds of the split:** JFB says Judah's claim of kinship was dangerous to David's house and sowed the seeds of later division. Same URL.
- **Pointing to Sheba (preceptaustin):** The north has just claimed ten shares, and in the next chapter Sheba turns it round: "no share in David." https://www.preceptaustin.org/2-samuel-20-commentary

## 2. Where commentators disagree

What I found are disagreements between individual commentators. I couldn't find statements from the denominations themselves.

**v. 23: Did David break his oath?**
- **Gill (Baptist, Calvinist):** The oath covered only that offence, and it didn't bind his successor. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-samuel/19-23.html
- **Poole (Puritan):** It meant "not by my hands." https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_samuel/19-23.htm
- **Cambridge Bible and the Pulpit Commentary (Anglican):** David can't be cleared of breaking at least the spirit of the oath. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_samuel/19-23.htm
- **Keil-Delitzsch (Lutheran scholars):** The pardon showed weakness, not real forgiveness. Same URL.
- **Ellicott:** David's oath was rash, and he kept it to the letter but no further. Same URL.
- **Kretzmann (Lutheran):** The pardon was mainly political, though signs of God's favour make believers glad to forgive. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-samuel/19-23.html

**v. 29: Fair settlement or injustice?**
- **Henry and Gill:** David was simply restoring his original arrangement. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-samuel/19-29.html
- **Geneva Study Bible (Reformed):** Taking the land was wrong, and failing to restore it once he knew the truth was "much worse." https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_samuel/19-29.htm
- **Keil-Delitzsch:** David didn't have the courage to take back his decree completely. Same URL.
- **Barnes, Pulpit and Poole:** All note political motives: David didn't want to make an enemy of the powerful Ziba. Same URL.
- **Desiring God (Baptist):** "It was not just and Mephibosheth knew it." https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/how-to-avoid-inheritance-disputes

## 3. Other views

- **Catholic, v. 43:** Haydock, citing Calmet, says the gap was nowhere near ten to one, so Israel's claim to the greater honour was unjust. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-samuel/19-43.html
- **Translation, v. 43:** The NET Bible renders the line "Why do you want to curse us?" (other versions: "despise us"). https://biblehub.com/2_samuel/19-43.htm
- **Early critical scholarship, Shimei's "house of Joseph" (vv. 19–20, background to v. 23):** Gill and Ellicott suggest the phrase might mean the passage was written after the kingdom split. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_samuel/19-23.htm
